items.title: Remove the deprecated bin aliases and prove nothing depends on them
items.context:
Delete bin/lattice.js and bin/lattice-codex.js. Do this LAST, after the rest is green, because it is the one irreversible break of the multi-developer compatibility guarantee B-cdf6 established. bin/proof-or-stop-codex.js references the codex alias and verify_codex has a check for it; both need updating. Also update the package.json bin map, the pre-push hook's self-repo detection, and CLAUDE.md.

INIT product-reviewer issue (medium): the original form of this item hard-cut the guarantee with NO transition signal, so a teammate would discover the break only when their 'lattice' invocation failed — a silent UX cliff. Amended acceptance: the removal must be ANNOUNCED, not merely performed. Required: a CHANGELOG entry naming both removed aliases and their replacements. PLAN must additionally decide between (a) a deprecation-warning phase where bin/lattice.js prints a visible notice before delegating, held one release cycle before removal, versus (b) immediate removal with the changelog as the only signal — and RECORD which was chosen and why. Option (a) is the reviewer's preference; the operator asked for removal, so the tradeoff is explicit rather than assumed.

items.title: Prove the state-directory move is reversible before performing it
items.context:
INIT-002, raised by the INIT reviewer and matching my own stated uncertainty: CHK-002's read-both resolver gives CODE-level reversibility but not DATA-move reversibility, and nothing covered aborting a partially-completed git mv of ~7574 tracked files. This item supplies the missing half. Establish and rehearse the abort procedure: confirm the move is a single atomic commit that 'git revert' undoes cleanly (git mv preserves content, so a revert restores paths without content loss), verify on a scratch clone that reverting restores story archives to a readable state, and record the exact abort command plus how to detect a half-done state.

SEQUENCING, corrected per INIT-005: this item's ID is CHK-008 because checklist_add appends, so its array POSITION is last — but it is an EXECUTION PREREQUISITE of CHK-003 (the git mv), not a follow-up. An earlier draft of this context claimed it was 'sequenced before CHK-003', which contradicted its own array position and was standalone-visible in checklist.json; that claim is withdrawn. The real ordering is enforced two ways: (1) PLAN must record CHK-003 DependsOn CHK-008 in plan.md, and (2) CHK-003 must not be started until this rehearsal is done and its evidence recorded. ID order is not execution order in this story.
items.userSees: rehearsal transcript shows `story_get` printing an archived story phase both after the move and after `git revert`, plus the exact abort command

happy.desc: On a scratch clone, story_get on an archived story succeeds BOTH after applying the move and after git revert

edge.desc: A deliberately half-done move (one dir moved, one not) is detected by the documented half-done check

adversarial.desc: The move is a single commit: git revert <sha> alone restores the pre-move layout with no manual fixup

verificationEvidence.note: CHK-008 apply-then-revert rehearsal COMPLETE on a scratch clone (344 archives). Measured: (1) git mv .lattice -> .proof-or-stop plus .lattice-codex -> .proof-or-stop-codex in ONE commit = 7610 files changed, 0 insertions, 0 deletions, and git show --name-status reports 7610/7610 status R (pure renames) — mechanical proof no archive CONTENT is rewritten. (2) A SINGLE git revert HEAD restores all 344 archives and both directories with a clean tree, so the abort path is one command. (3) git log --follow on .lattice/story/actives/B-0168/background.md still traces 3 commits after move+revert, proving history follows the rename. (4) HALF-DONE DETECTION: exactly one of .lattice / .proof-or-stop present = consistent state; BOTH present simultaneously = half-done move, abort. ABORT COMMAND for CHK-003: git revert --no-edit <move-sha>.
verificationEvidence.nonMechanicalReason: Rehearsal was performed on a throwaway git clone outside this worktree, so it cannot be re-executed as a pinned in-repo command without re-cloning 7610 files. Full transcript recorded here and in the contract doc; the assertions it establishes are re-checkable at CHK-003 execution time against the real move.
